title: Seven Countries Drive Most UK Study Visa Refusals as 5% Cap Reshapes Admissions
excerpt: Home Office data to June 2026 show refusals concentrated in Pakistan, Nigeria and India, with universities withdrawing offers to protect their sponsor licences under the tightened compliance threshold.
body:
• In the year to June 2026, the UK issued 83,958 student visas to Indian applicants and refused 3,846 — a 4.4 per cent published refusal rate, rising to 6.2 per cent with withdrawals counted, Home Office data analysed by The PIE News show.
  • Pakistan (4,778 refusals), Nigeria (4,344) and India (3,846) top the refusal counts; across all markets there were 19,608 refusals on 383,455 issued visas.
  • Universities must now keep refusal rates below 5 per cent under the tightened Basic Compliance Assessment, down from 10 per cent, alongside 95 per cent enrolment and 85 per cent completion thresholds.
  • Indian applications fell 31 per cent in the first half of 2026 and visas issued fell 36 per cent; before paying a deposit, check your university's sponsor compliance position.

A small group of countries accounts for the overwhelming share of UK study visa refusals, and the concentration is now reshaping which students British universities are willing to sponsor at all. Home Office data for the year ending June 2026, analysed by The PIE News, show 19,608 refusals across all markets against 383,455 visas issued. Pakistan led with 4,778 refusals, followed by Nigeria with 4,344 and India with 3,846; Bangladesh, Ghana and Nepal add most of the remainder.

Why universities are pulling offers

The mechanism is the Basic Compliance Assessment. Since June 1, institutions sponsoring foreign students must keep visa refusal rates below 5 per cent — tightened from 10 per cent — enrol at least 95 per cent of sponsored students and achieve an 85 per cent course-completion rate, or risk losing their sponsor licence. The PIE describes the result as self-regulation: universities and agents managing the number the licence is judged on, one application at a time. Withdrawals are the tell. Pakistan and Nigeria between them account for 57 per cent of the year's 11,500 withdrawals, and in the first quarter of 2026 Pakistan's refusal rate read 39.3 per cent on the published basis and 65.3 per cent with withdrawals counted.

Around 15 universities are reported to have suspended recruitment from Pakistan this year, and institutions have curtailed recruitment from other higher-refusal markets, according to reporting on the Financial Times analysis. Universities say a withdrawn application is not always a student changing their mind: institutions revoke offers pre-emptively to protect compliance records, and processing delays mean some students withdraw because a decision never arrived before their start date.

Where India stands

India's published refusal rate, 4.4 per cent, sits just under the 5 per cent threshold that matters to sponsors — but the trend is adverse. Indian withdrawal rates climbed from 1.2 per cent in January-June 2025 to 5.2 per cent in the same period of 2026, applications fell 31 per cent and visas issued fell 36 per cent, according to the ICEF Monitor analysis. Some universities are reportedly shifting recruitment focus toward China and India as lower-risk markets, even as India's own numbers worsen.

For an Indian applicant, the practical consequence is concrete: your admission offer is no longer solely about your file — it is also about your university's aggregate refusal rate, a number you cannot see in real time and the university itself says UKVI does not share promptly. Before paying a deposit, ask the university directly about its BCA status and whether your course intake is affected by recruitment pauses; an offer withdrawn for compliance reasons costs you a cycle, not just a fee.
